main_text.p: ter dictam victus rationem magis exquisita: ut, ceratum de pelle arietis Matth. Gradi, cui simile est emplastrum contra ruptură Nicolai. Sunt qui ferro candenti partem qua descendit intestinum vrendo contrahunt: aliĭ acu & filo advsque cauitatem qua descendunt vasa, carnem pertundunt: ablata acu filum super tessellam corneam vel eburneam astringunt quotidie magis atq; magis, donec totum filo perruperint: carne interim supercrescente in profundo, & meatus partem occupante, ne intestino postea sit via: sed caue ne & vasa cicatrice interna, dura, & eminentiore premas: nam dolorifica sic fuerit, et testem atrophia tabefecerit. Alij sectione fa Eta, execloque teste, vinculo vasorum omnium, & ambientis membranae, aut cauterio meatum contrahunt, & obturant: in qua castratione grandes natu plerique oris primum, deinde corporis reliqui conuulsione tandē moriuntur: pueris alia inde accidunt incommoda non exigua. Ob id hæc curandi forma potius omittenda est.

page.notes: Left margin note: "Vide Alexandrum benedicti um", set beside the lines "totum filo" to "crescente". Catchword "EPI-" appears at the foot right as a hyphenated word beginning the next page. Some words are uncertain in the dense Latin, notably "castratione" and "Eta"; the text was read from the scan with care but may contain small errors.
